overall: Atlanta is in the pre-dawn hours with a current temperature of 75.2°F and a running max already at 82.4°F, reflecting a very warm overnight minimum driven by an extremely high dewpoint of 71.6°F — near-oppressive moisture that is suppressing overnight cooling and preconditioning the atmosphere for significant daytime heating. The -3.3°F/hr velocity is consistent with a typical early-morning radiative cooling trough and is not a concern for the daytime outlook. The high moisture load and light winds point to a hot, humid afternoon.
forecast_obs_notes: Models are in reasonable agreement, clustering in two sub-groups: GFS and HRRR are locked in at 93.3°F, while ECMWF and NBM are slightly cooler at 91.0°F and 91.4°F respectively — a spread of about 2.3°F across the full suite. The Tier 1 odd-model ensemble signal at 93–94°F with 27% peak-bin confidence corroborates the GFS/HRRR guidance, while the even-model signal at 90–91°F carries only 14% confidence and is rated Tier 4 (Avoid), reducing its weight materially.
max_temp_prediction: The preponderance of evidence — GFS/HRRR agreement at 93.3°F, the Tier 1 odd-model ensemble pointing to 93–94°F, and the extremely high boundary-layer moisture (dewpoint 71.6°F) that will drive robust afternoon convective mixing — supports a daily high in the 92–93°F range. The ECMWF/NBM pull toward 91°F introduces modest downside risk, likely tied to cloud or convective-cap uncertainty, but the dominant signal is for the upper end. Confidence is moderately high given model consensus and the strong ensemble tier signal.
